implement: legion-worker: the phase contract this change is delivered under — the handoff, the pushes, and references/pr-body.md, which is the sole definition of the E2E (implementer) line and the six-field proof entries this issue's two proofs (the live plugin run and the CI browser runs) must take.
legion-worker/references/pr-body.md: also the simplify pass and the rule that a unit test is never a proof, which decides how the plugin half's live run is recorded.

ce-simplify-code: the simplify pass pr-body.md requires on the settled head before the implementer completes; this change touches a long-lived React row and a precedence chain in session-title.ts, both easy to leave more complicated than needed.
dispatch-first: search before posting anything, and the rule that a finding outside this issue is a dispatch ask (INFRA-95 is changing the same two Dispatch files).
dispatch: every Dispatch write this phase makes, including any question to the architect's decision path, follows its command and writing rules.
test: legion-worker: the tester's charter — drive the application rather than re-run CI, and write the test handoff with implementerProof, failures and its own proof.

legion-worker/references/pr-body.md: what the tester verifies in the implementer's proof lines and what its own E2E (tester) line and proof array must hold; it also says the static checks (lint, types, unit suites) are CI's and are not re-run here.
dispatch-first: search before opening any ask, and findings outside this issue go to a dispatch ask, never a new issue.
dispatch: the rules for any Dispatch write the tester makes.
review: legion-worker: the reviewer's phase order — read the code commit's checks on GitHub, push the handoff, review the head that push made, then complete.

legion-worker/references/review-threads.md: one disposition reply per thread, resolved one by one, and how a bot's finding is adjudicated; this pull request will carry browser-suite and plugin findings from two reviewers.
legion-worker/references/merge-gate.md: what an approval of a head by SHA means here, since READY compares the approved head with the merge head.
dispatch: any Dispatch write the reviewer makes follows it.

findings.finding: F1 — the spec never says how a hook process, which exits in milliseconds, hands the chosen name to the already-running channel server; three mechanisms with different latency and risk.
findings.answer: Plan A1/A3: a state file the hook writes and the registration reads, with no new watcher. The rename rides the existing two-minute heartbeat, which is exactly what the spec promises. Widening the existing session-id handoff file was rejected: readSessionHandoff would make an older installed dist adopt the new format as a session id.

findings.finding: F2 — the state's key is unstated and silently decides /clear, claude --resume, concurrent sessions and cleanup.
findings.answer: Plan A1: keyed by session id (titles/<url-encoded id>), so a resume finds the name and a /clear cannot inherit one, and it does not rest on the hook and the server sharing a parent pid. Because nothing prunes an id-keyed file today, the plan adds pruneStaleSessionTitles (thirty days) beside the existing handoff prune.

findings.finding: F3 — packages/dispatch/e2e/phone.e2e.ts:757-761 asserts the Agents row's name ellipsises, and it runs in the chromium profile too, so Half B contradicts a passing test the spec never mentions.
findings.answer: Plan B1: that assertion is narrowed to the iphone profile in the same commit, named as part of Half B's work.

findings.finding: F4 — whether the name must also show whole on a phone.
findings.answer: Plan B1 decides it does not: the spec sizes the name at a laptop's width and asks of a phone only the whole path, and a 64-character name needs about four lines in a 390-pixel row. Named in the completion summary so the architect can overturn it; it is a one-class change plus deleting the narrowed assertion.

findings.finding: F5 — nothing bounds a title's length, and the spec gives no behaviour for a name far longer than 64 characters.
findings.answer: Plan decision 5: no cap and no line clamp (the suite's own assertWhole helper fails on any clamp). The browser row instead seeds a second session whose 64-character name has no spaces and asserts assertPageFits, so an unbreakable name cannot widen the page.

findings.finding: F6 — the spec does not state what the new UserPromptSubmit hook may do, and that hook runs before every prompt.
findings.answer: Plan A2: silent on stdout, always exit 0, local file work only, timeout 5 s, synchronous rather than async: true because Claude Code kills async hooks at teardown in -p mode and every Legion Claude worker runs claude -p. tests/hooks-timeout.test.ts gains the entry. Measured cost: the bundle's dispatch-first mode runs in 165 ms in this pod and the title mode does less.

findings.finding: F7 — what happens when a payload carries no chosen title after one did.
findings.answer: Plan A3, decision 2: the record is removed and the fallback returns. Claude Code's hooks reference says session_title is 'present when one is set', so absence means no custom title; a rename can therefore be undone, and no unnamed session holds a stale name.

findings.finding: F8 — the spec's attribution sentence holds only for sessions that register; with Envoy or inbound messages off the title is stamped once at startup.
findings.answer: Plan A3 and decision 9: those two paths pick up a chosen name present when they start, and a later rename does not reach them. That is today's behaviour for every title, is recorded so the next phase does not read it as a regression, and is reported to the architect.

findings.finding: F9 — 'keeps the whole path' on a phone, the machine name's fate, and the exact hover string are all unstated.
findings.answer: Plan B2: on a phone the full '<machine> · <path>' is shown and stops being clipped, since there is no hover there; on a laptop the row shows '<machine> · <last segment>' with title='<machine> · <full path>'. The machine name stays — the spec shortens the directory, not the row.

findings.finding: F10 — precedence and cleaning of the chosen name: short id, blank, invisible, multi-line, ANSI or bidi.
findings.answer: Plan A3 and decisions 3 and 4: ENVOY_SESSION_TITLE first and short-circuiting, then the chosen name alone with no short id, cleaned by the existing oneLine and accepted only when visible(), else today's fallback. Covered by rows in tests/session-title.test.ts.

findings.finding: F11 — the claim that Legion's Claude workers are renamed as they start is not shown by the code: the daemon sends /rename as a user message and a resumed pane is never seeded.
findings.answer: Plan A4 states what follows and what does not: the name lands on the pane's next prompt, one prompt later than 'as they start', and a resumed pane keeps its custom title through the SessionStart payload. That a slash command arriving on stream-json input renames the session is Claude Code's behaviour, unrunnable in this pod, and is reported to the architect rather than asserted.

findings.finding: F12 — four claims about Claude Code and live data that nothing in the repository shows, among them the payload field's name and semantics, which block the hook's schema.
findings.answer: Resolved from Claude Code's own hooks reference (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks), quoted in the plan: SessionStart receives session_title, 'the session's custom title, present when one is set, for example with --name, /rename, a hook's sessionTitle output, or the Agent SDK's renameSession()', and 'UserPromptSubmit hooks also receive session_title when the session has a custom title, with the same meaning'. The parent-pid worry is removed by the id keying (F2). The 64-character figure is the spec's own measurement of live data and is not re-measured.

findings.finding: F13 — 'fails before the change and passes after it ... from the repository's own checks' cannot be met by one branch state, and this pod cannot run the suite.
findings.answer: Plan 'Order of work': two pushes on the pull request — the browser row alone, which the dispatch job fails in both profiles, then the implementation, which it passes. Both runs quoted on the pull request, as the architect's comment on this issue sets out. The phase is completed only at the green head.

findings.finding: F14 — the spec's Half A proof is the plugin's own tests, while the architect requires a live run; it is unstated whether that run is a committed script and what counts as simulated.
findings.answer: Plan 'The live run of the plugin half': a committed packages/claude-envoy/scripts/smoke-session-title.sh beside the package's two existing manual smokes, excluded from CI, so the tester re-runs exactly what the implementer ran; its negative control is the base commit's dist. The simulated part is named in the script header, the plan, the handoff and the pull request: Claude Code is not installed in an issue pod, so the two hook payloads are JSON the script writes in the documented shape.

findings.finding: F15 — five acceptance lines no machine can check as written (the two-minute latency, 'shows in full', 'on hover', the attribution claim, the Legion-worker claim).
findings.answer: The plan's acceptance table replaces each with a surface and a command: the listener's GET /v1/sessions after each recorded name; assertWhole plus assertPageFits at 1280 pixels; the directory span's title attribute compared with the exact full string; the stamped <DISPATCH_STATE_DIR>/sessions/<id>/title file; and the Legion-worker line kept as background (A4), not acceptance.

findings.finding: F16 — documentation that states today's behaviour and becomes wrong is not named in the spec.
findings.answer: Plan A6 names them: packages/claude-envoy/AGENTS.md (the hook row and the Session title row), README.md's precedence list and CHANGELOG.md. packages/dispatch/AGENTS.md is reviewed for any sentence about the Agents row's truncation.

findings.finding: F17 — the spec says INFRA-95 is changing another test in the same browser suite; the analyst could not read Dispatch.
findings.answer: Read here: dispatch://INFRA-95 changes packages/dispatch/e2e/phone.e2e.ts:393 ('an inline link keeps its line'), packages/dispatch/web/src/styles.css and packages/dispatch/AGENTS.md. INFRA-92 edits different rows of phone.e2e.ts and AGENTS.md, so the collision is textual only; the plan's Risks section says whichever lands second brings its base in as a forward merge and re-runs the suite.
